claims.text: Continuous integration is the practice of merging small changes into the shared main branch often, with every change built and tested automatically.
claims.source_hint: glossary continuous-integration; GitHub Docs: About continuous integration with GitHub Actions

claims.text: The default branch of the Đơn Hàng repository is master.

claims.text: ci.yml@stage-1 lines 3-6: on: push:, pull_request:, workflow_dispatch: with no filters: a run starts on every push to any branch and when a pull request is opened or updated (opened/synchronize/reopened), not if the PR has a merge conflict.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1 .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6; GitHub Docs: Events that trigger workflows (push, pull_request)

claims.text: For the pull_request event, the run's commit (GITHUB_SHA) is the merge commit GitHub creates for the pull request (refs/pull/N/merge), i.e. the result of merging the head branch into the base branch; actions/checkout checks that out by default.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Events that trigger workflows > pull_request (GITHUB_SHA / GITHUB_REF); actions/checkout README

claims.text: GitHub Actions (GitHub's CI service) reads workflow files in .github/workflows/; with runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 each run's job starts on a new GitHub-hosted VM; files not in the commit are not there; actions/checkout copies the commit's files onto it.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About GitHub-hosted runners (fresh instance per job); actions/checkout

claims.text: actions/setup-dotnet@v4 with global-json-file: global.json makes sure the machine has an SDK that global.json accepts (10.0.300, rollForward latestFeature: 10.0.300 or a later 10.0 SDK); the .NET SDK is the dotnet command and its compiler.

SDK-style projects compile every **/*.cs file under the project folder by default, tracked by Git or not; DonHang.Domain.csproj@stage-1 does not change this, so an untracked Scratch.cs is compiled on the laptop.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs docs/core/project-sdk/overview.md (Default includes and excludes); examples/don-hang @ stage-1 DonHang.Domain/DonHang.Domain.csproj

claims.text: ci.yml@stage-1 lines 25-29 run dotnet build DonHang.slnx --warnaserror (compiler warnings become errors) then dotnet test DonHang.slnx --no-build (test without building again, reusing the previous build).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1 .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-29; .NET docs: dotnet build (-warnaserror), dotnet test (--no-build)

claims.text: A CI result is reported for one commit: a green run says that commit built and passed its checks; a later commit gets its own run and result.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: About status checks (checks are attached to a commit SHA); Viewing workflow run history

claims.text: git status --short marks an untracked file with ??, e.g. '?? DonHang.Domain/Scratch.cs'; .gitignore at stage-1 does not ignore DonHang.Domain/*.cs.
claims.source_hint: git-status docs (Short Format: ?? untracked); examples/don-hang @ stage-1 .gitignore

claims.text: Merging small changes often keeps each integration small, so a broken combination is found soon after it is made, when the team runs CI on every change.
claims.source_hint: outline item 1; GitHub Docs: About continuous integration

claims.text: A pull_request run builds the merge commit as of when it runs; a change that reaches master after that run is not in it, and the next push to master starts a run on the commit that combines both.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Docs: Events that trigger workflows > pull_request (GITHUB_SHA = last merge commit), push
